newsitem.title: LEBANON: BLC, Solidere rise in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: BLC, Solidere rise in Beirut.

text.p: Shares in Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce (BLC) rose on Monday for the fourth successive trading day on the Beirut Stock Exchange, closing at $12 from $11.75 on Friday.
Solidere also rose after its 10-for-one stock split took effect on Monday. A shares rose to $11.25 from $11.2 ($112 before the split) and B shares rose to $11.625 from $11.5 ($115 before split).

BLC, the first bank listed on the Beirut exchange since it reopened a year ago, gave a star performance on its first week of trading, closing at $11.75 on Friday from $11.50 on Thursday and $11.25 on Monday when they began trading.
However, BLC turnover on Monday fell to 1,500 shares -- the lowest since they began trading. On Friday 10,000 shares changed hands against Thursday's 5,000 and last Monday's 2,000.
Turnover in Solidere rose after the stock split to 24,120 shares against 2,058 for a value of $272,265 from $232,107.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index percent rose 0.22 percent to 81.94 and the BLOM stock index rose 0.66 percent to 954.26.
